chapters.title: Computer Fundamentals
chapters.desc: What a computer is, how it works, and basic terms.

questions.q: What does CPU stand for?
questions.e: CPU means Central Processing Unit. It executes instructions.

questions.q: Which of these is an input device?
questions.e: A keyboard sends user input into the computer.

questions.q: Which device is mainly an output device?
questions.e: A monitor displays output from the computer.

questions.q: Which part is often called the brain of the computer?
questions.e: The CPU processes instructions, so it is often called the computer's brain.

questions.q: What is the smallest unit of data in a computer?
questions.e: A bit is the smallest unit and stores 0 or 1.

questions.q: What is the main difference between hardware and software?
o: Hardware is physical; software is programs
Hardware is free; software is paid
Hardware is online; software is offline
Hardware is data; software is electricity
questions.e: Hardware is the physical equipment. Software is the set of programs and instructions.

questions.q: Which of these is system software?
questions.e: An operating system is system software because it manages the computer.

questions.q: Which memory loses its contents when power is turned off?
questions.e: RAM is volatile memory, so its contents are lost without power.

questions.q: How many bits are in one byte?
questions.e: One byte contains 8 bits.

questions.q: Which device can work as both an input and output device?
questions.e: A touchscreen shows output and also accepts touch input.

questions.q: Which computer generation is associated with microprocessors?
questions.e: Fourth-generation computers used microprocessors.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly describes the basic CPU cycle?
questions.e: The CPU repeatedly fetches an instruction, decodes it, and executes it.

questions.q: Which register holds the address of the next instruction to execute?
questions.e: The program counter stores the address of the next instruction.

questions.q: What is the main job of the ALU?
questions.e: The Arithmetic Logic Unit performs calculations and logical comparisons.

questions.q: What is firmware?
o: Software stored on hardware such as ROM
questions.e: Firmware is software embedded in hardware, commonly stored in non-volatile memory.

chapters.title: Hardware & Devices
chapters.desc: CPU, memory, storage, ports, and physical devices.

questions.q: Which device prints documents?
questions.e: A printer produces paper output from digital documents.

questions.q: Which device is used to point and click?
questions.e: A mouse is a pointing device.

questions.q: What is the main circuit board inside a computer called?
questions.e: The motherboard connects the CPU, memory, storage, and other components.

questions.q: Which component is temporary working memory?
questions.e: RAM is temporary working memory used while programs run.

questions.q: Which device is used for long-term file storage?
questions.e: A hard disk drive stores files long term.

questions.q: Why are SSDs usually faster than HDDs?
o: They have no moving mechanical parts
questions.e: SSDs use flash memory and do not rely on moving read/write heads.

questions.q: What is PCIe mainly used for?
questions.e: PCI Express connects devices such as graphics cards and NVMe storage.

questions.q: What does a PSU do?
o: Converts mains power for computer components
questions.e: The power supply unit converts AC power to the DC voltages components need.

questions.q: Which component connects a computer to a network?
questions.e: A network interface card or controller provides network connectivity.

questions.q: Which component is designed mainly for graphics processing?
questions.e: A graphics processing unit renders images and handles parallel graphics work.

questions.q: In older PC architecture, which chip connected the CPU to fast components such as RAM and graphics?
questions.e: The northbridge handled high-speed links such as memory and graphics.

questions.q: What does POST check?
questions.e: The Power-On Self-Test checks essential hardware before the operating system loads.

questions.q: Why does a motherboard use a CMOS battery?
o: To keep firmware settings and the real-time clock when power is off
questions.e: The small battery preserves settings and time when the computer is unplugged.

questions.q: What does RAID 1 provide?
questions.e: RAID 1 mirrors data on two disks so one disk can fail without losing the data.

questions.q: Which storage interface is designed for very fast SSDs connected over PCIe?
questions.e: NVMe is a storage protocol built for flash storage over PCI Express.

chapters.title: Software & Operating Systems
chapters.desc: Programs, operating systems, processes, and memory management.

questions.q: Which of these is an operating system?
questions.e: Linux is an operating system kernel used by many operating systems.

questions.q: Which of these is application software?
questions.e: A web browser is an application used directly by people.

questions.q: Which file extension normally means a plain text file?
questions.e: A .txt file normally contains plain text.

questions.q: What is a folder used for?
questions.e: Folders organise files and other folders.

questions.q: Which keyboard shortcut copies selected text?
questions.e: Ctrl+C copies the selected item.

questions.q: What is the main job of an operating system?
o: Manage hardware, software, files, and users
questions.e: The operating system manages resources and provides services to applications.

questions.q: What does a compiler do?
o: Translates a whole high-level program into machine code
questions.e: A compiler translates source code into an executable form, usually before it runs.

questions.q: How does an interpreter usually run code?
o: Line by line or statement by statement
questions.e: An interpreter executes source code step by step without first building one whole executable.

questions.q: What is a process?
questions.e: A process is a program that is currently running.

questions.q: What does multitasking allow?
o: Several tasks to share CPU time
The monitor to show two colors only
questions.e: Multitasking lets the operating system switch between tasks so several appear to run together.

questions.q: What is virtual memory?
o: Disk space used as an extension of RAM
questions.e: Virtual memory lets the system move inactive pages to storage so programs can use more memory than physical RAM.

questions.q: What is the kernel?
o: The core part of the operating system
questions.e: The kernel manages low-level resources such as CPU, memory, devices, and system calls.

questions.q: What is a deadlock?
o: Processes waiting forever for each other's resources
questions.e: Deadlock happens when processes hold resources and wait in a cycle for each other.

questions.q: What is thrashing in an operating system?
o: Too much paging and too little useful work
questions.e: Thrashing occurs when the system spends most of its time moving memory pages instead of running programs.

questions.q: Which OS component decides which ready process runs next?
questions.e: The CPU scheduler chooses the next process or thread to run.

chapters.title: Memory & Storage
chapters.desc: RAM, ROM, cache, disks, units, and RAID.

questions.q: Which memory is volatile?
questions.e: RAM loses its data when power is removed.

questions.q: Which memory is normally non-volatile?
questions.e: ROM keeps its contents without power.

questions.q: Which memory is usually the fastest in a computer?
questions.e: Cache memory is much faster than main storage and sits close to the CPU.

questions.q: What does SSD stand for?
questions.e: SSD means Solid State Drive.

questions.q: Which device is commonly used as portable storage?
questions.e: A USB flash drive is portable storage.

questions.q: In binary computer units, how many bytes are in 1 KiB?
questions.e: One kibibyte (KiB) is 1024 bytes. Many people informally say kilobyte.

questions.q: What is virtual memory used for?
questions.e: Virtual memory uses disk space to supplement physical RAM.

questions.q: Which pair is primary memory?
questions.e: RAM and ROM are primary memory directly used by the system.

questions.q: Which of these is secondary storage?
questions.e: An SSD is persistent secondary storage.

questions.q: Which memory type is commonly used in USB flash drives?
questions.e: USB drives commonly use non-volatile flash memory.

questions.q: Which cache level is usually smallest and fastest?
questions.e: L1 cache is closest to the CPU core and is usually the smallest and fastest.

questions.q: Why does DRAM need refreshing?
questions.e: DRAM cells store charge that leaks, so the memory controller refreshes them.

questions.q: Which is generally faster, SRAM or DRAM?
questions.e: SRAM is faster and more expensive; DRAM is denser and used for main memory.

questions.q: What does RAID 0 provide?
questions.e: RAID 0 stripes data across disks for performance, but one disk failure can lose the array.

questions.q: What does wear leveling do in an SSD?
o: Spreads writes to extend flash life
questions.e: Wear leveling distributes writes across flash cells so no small area wears out too quickly.

chapters.title: Number System & Data
chapters.desc: Binary, decimal, octal, hexadecimal, and character data.

questions.q: Which digits are used in binary?
questions.e: Binary uses only 0 and 1.

questions.q: What is the base of the decimal number system?
questions.e: Decimal is base 10.

questions.q: Which symbols are used in hexadecimal?
questions.e: Hexadecimal uses digits 0 to 9 and letters A to F.

questions.q: What is the base of the octal number system?
questions.e: Octal is base 8.

questions.q: What is one bit?
questions.e: A bit stores one binary digit: 0 or 1.

questions.q: What is binary 1010 in decimal?
questions.e: 1010 binary is 8 + 2 = 10.

questions.q: What is decimal 15 in hexadecimal?
questions.e: Hexadecimal F represents decimal 15.

questions.q: What is binary 1111 in decimal?
What is octal 10 in decimal?
questions.e: Octal 10 means one group of 8, so it is decimal 8.

questions.q: How many bits are in one nibble?
questions.e: A nibble contains 4 bits.

questions.q: Which representation is commonly used for signed binary integers?
questions.e: Modern computers commonly use two's complement for signed integers.

questions.q: What is binary 1011 + 0110?
questions.e: Binary 1011 is 11 and 0110 is 6; their sum is 17, which is 10001.

questions.q: What is hexadecimal 2F in decimal?
What is octal 17 in decimal?
questions.e: Octal 17 is 1 x 8 + 7 = 15.

questions.q: What is the ASCII decimal value of uppercase A?
questions.e: ASCII represents uppercase A as decimal 65.

chapters.title: Computer Networking Basics
chapters.desc: LANs, IP addresses, common devices, and protocols.

questions.q: What does LAN stand for?
questions.e: LAN means Local Area Network.

questions.q: Which device connects different networks together?
questions.e: A router forwards traffic between different networks.

questions.q: Which device traditionally connects a home network to an ISP line?
questions.e: A modem connects the local network to the provider's line.

questions.q: What does an IP address help identify?
questions.e: An IP address identifies a network interface so traffic can reach it.

questions.q: What is Wi-Fi used for?
questions.e: Wi-Fi provides wireless network access.

questions.q: What does DNS translate?
questions.e: DNS resolves names like example.com to IP addresses.

questions.q: Which protocol is connection-oriented and reliable?
questions.e: TCP creates a connection and provides ordered, reliable delivery.

questions.q: Which protocol is faster but does not guarantee delivery?
questions.e: UDP sends datagrams without TCP's delivery and ordering guarantees.

questions.q: What is a MAC address?
o: A hardware address for a network interface
questions.e: A MAC address identifies a network interface on the local link.

questions.q: Which device forwards frames inside a LAN using MAC addresses?
questions.e: A switch learns MAC addresses and forwards frames to the right port.

questions.q: How many layers does the OSI model have?
questions.e: The OSI reference model has seven layers.

questions.q: What does a subnet mask help separate?
o: Network and host portions of an IP address
questions.e: The subnet mask shows which part of an IPv4 address is the network prefix.

questions.q: Which service assigns IP settings automatically?
questions.e: DHCP assigns IP addresses, gateways, DNS servers, and related settings.

questions.q: What is a default gateway used for?
o: Sending traffic to destinations outside the local network
questions.e: Hosts send non-local traffic to their default gateway, usually a router.

questions.q: What does NAT commonly do?
o: Translates private addresses to a public address
questions.e: Network Address Translation lets many private devices share public address space.

chapters.title: Internet & Web
chapters.desc: Browsers, URLs, websites, email, and web safety.

questions.q: What does WWW stand for?
questions.e: WWW means World Wide Web.

questions.q: Which of these is a web browser?
questions.e: Google Chrome is a web browser.

questions.q: What is a URL?
o: The address of a web resource
questions.e: A URL is the address used to locate a resource on the web.

questions.q: Which of these is a search engine?
questions.e: Google is a search engine.

questions.q: What does email mean?
questions.e: Email is electronic mail sent over a network.

questions.q: Which protocol is the foundation of web browsing?
questions.e: Web browsers use HTTP to request and receive web resources.

questions.q: What does HTTPS add to HTTP?
o: Encryption and server authentication through TLS
questions.e: HTTPS protects web traffic with TLS.

questions.q: Which language defines the structure of a web page?
questions.e: HTML is the markup language used to structure web pages.

questions.q: What does an ISP provide?
questions.e: An Internet Service Provider provides internet connectivity.

questions.q: What does downloading mean?
o: Receiving a file from another system
Sending a file to another system only
questions.e: Downloading copies data from a remote system to your device.

questions.q: Which URL part usually identifies the website domain?
questions.e: In https://example.com/home, example.com is the domain.

questions.q: What are browser cookies mainly used for?
o: Storing small pieces of site data in the browser
questions.e: Cookies let websites store state such as login sessions or preferences.

questions.q: Why does a browser use cache?
o: To reuse downloaded resources and load pages faster
questions.e: Caching keeps copies of images and other resources so repeat visits are faster.

questions.q: Which service lets people use names instead of IP addresses on the web?
questions.e: DNS maps domain names to IP addresses.

questions.q: What is phishing?
o: Fraudulent messages that try to steal information
questions.e: Phishing uses fake messages or sites to trick people into revealing information.

chapters.title: MS Office & Productivity
chapters.desc: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and common shortcuts.

questions.q: Which Office app is mainly for documents?
questions.e: Microsoft Word is used for documents.

questions.q: Which Office app is mainly for spreadsheets?
questions.e: Excel is a spreadsheet application.

questions.q: Which Office app is mainly for presentations?
questions.e: PowerPoint creates slide presentations.

questions.q: Which shortcut saves a file?
questions.e: Ctrl+S saves the current file.

questions.q: Which shortcut opens print options?
questions.e: Ctrl+P opens printing in most applications.

questions.q: How does a formula usually begin in Excel?
questions.e: Excel formulas begin with an equals sign.

questions.q: Which Excel function adds values?
questions.e: SUM adds numbers in a range.

questions.q: What is Mail Merge used for in Word?
o: Creating personalised letters or labels for many recipients
questions.e: Mail Merge combines a document with a data source to create personalised copies.

questions.q: What is a transition in PowerPoint?
questions.e: A transition controls how one slide changes to the next.

questions.q: What is a cell in Excel?
o: The intersection of a row and a column
questions.e: A cell is where a row and column meet in a worksheet.

questions.q: Which Excel reference stays fixed when copied?
questions.e: $A$1 is an absolute reference; both column and row stay fixed.

questions.q: What does VLOOKUP search?
o: The first column of a table and returns a value from another column
questions.e: VLOOKUP looks down the first column and returns a matching value from a chosen column.

questions.q: Which Excel function makes a decision based on a condition?
questions.e: IF returns one value when a condition is true and another when it is false.

questions.q: What does Presenter View in PowerPoint show the presenter?
o: Current slide, next slide, and speaker notes
questions.e: Presenter View gives the speaker controls, notes, and the next slide while the audience sees the current slide.

questions.q: Why would you use a section break in Word?
o: To apply different layout or formatting to different parts of a document
questions.e: Section breaks let one document use different headers, margins, columns, or page numbering.

chapters.title: Computer Security
chapters.desc: Passwords, malware, encryption, backups, and safe habits.

questions.q: What should a password be?
questions.e: A password should be private and difficult for others to guess.

questions.q: What is antivirus software used for?
questions.e: Antivirus software helps detect, block, and remove malicious software.

questions.q: What is a phishing message trying to do?
questions.e: Phishing messages pretend to be trustworthy to steal credentials or information.

questions.q: Why should you keep a backup?
o: To recover data if the original is lost
questions.e: Backups let you restore files after deletion, damage, or device failure.

questions.q: Why are software updates important?
o: They fix bugs and security holes
questions.e: Updates patch vulnerabilities and improve reliability.

questions.q: What does 2FA add to a password?
questions.e: Two-factor authentication requires another factor, such as a code or device.

questions.q: What does a firewall do?
o: Filters network traffic based on rules
questions.e: A firewall allows or blocks traffic according to configured rules.

questions.q: What is malware?
questions.e: Malware is software designed to harm, spy, steal, or disrupt.

questions.q: Which is the strongest password habit?
o: Use long unique passwords for important accounts
questions.e: Long, unique passwords reduce the damage if one account is exposed.

questions.q: What does encryption do?
o: Turns readable data into protected data that needs a key
questions.e: Encryption protects confidentiality by requiring a key to read the data.

questions.q: What does ransomware do?
questions.e: Ransomware locks or steals data and demands payment.

questions.q: What is social engineering?
questions.e: Social engineering attacks human trust instead of only technical systems.

questions.q: What is the main property of a cryptographic hash?
o: It is designed to be one-way
It stores passwords as plain text
questions.e: A cryptographic hash should be impractical to reverse.

questions.q: What does the principle of least privilege mean?
o: Give only the access needed for the task
questions.e: Least privilege limits damage by giving users and programs only required access.

questions.q: What is the main idea of Zero Trust security?
questions.e: Zero Trust verifies users, devices, and requests instead of trusting a network location by default.

chapters.title: Troubleshooting & IT Essentials
chapters.desc: Safe diagnosis and common fixes for everyday computer problems.

questions.q: What is a safe first step for many temporary computer problems?
questions.e: A restart clears many temporary software states and is a safe first step.

questions.q: If a monitor shows nothing, what should you check first?
questions.e: A loose power or display cable is a common cause of no display.

questions.q: Which Windows tool can end an unresponsive app?
questions.e: Task Manager shows running apps and can end a frozen process.

questions.q: What does Safe Mode do?
o: Starts the system with minimal drivers and services
questions.e: Safe Mode starts a minimal environment for troubleshooting.

questions.q: What should you do before a risky repair?
questions.e: A backup protects data before making major changes.

questions.q: What can cause a Windows blue screen error?
o: Faulty drivers, hardware, or system files
questions.e: Blue screens often come from driver, hardware, or low-level system faults.

questions.q: If a PC becomes slow at startup, what should you check?
questions.e: Too many startup programs can slow boot and sign-in.

questions.q: What is a sensible first check when internet stops working?
o: Restart or check the router and connection
questions.e: Router and connection checks quickly rule out common network problems.

questions.q: If a printer is offline, what should you check first?
questions.e: Printer offline problems often come from power, cable/network, or stuck jobs.

questions.q: What can you safely do when a disk is almost full?
o: Remove unneeded files or uninstall unused apps
questions.e: Freeing space by removing unneeded files or apps is safe and reversible compared with deleting system files.

questions.q: What does the Windows SFC tool do?
o: Scans and repairs protected system files
questions.e: System File Checker scans protected Windows system files and can repair corrupted copies.

questions.q: What does the ping command test?
questions.e: Ping sends ICMP echo requests to check basic reachability and delay.

questions.q: Where does Windows record many system and application events?
questions.e: Event Viewer shows Windows and application logs useful for diagnosis.

questions.q: What is a clean boot used for?
o: Starting Windows with minimal services and startup apps to isolate conflicts
questions.e: A clean boot disables non-Microsoft services and startup items to find software conflicts.

questions.q: What does System Restore do?
o: Rolls system settings and files back to an earlier restore point
questions.e: System Restore can return Windows system state to a previous point without being a full backup replacement.
